prompt.content:
You are generating synthetic enterprise support ticket text for a dataset used to train and evaluate support-case classification systems. For each case in the input JSON array, write a realistic support ticket TITLE and DESCRIPTION as the customer would write it — not as an engineer would describe the internal diagnosis.

Vary sentence structure, technical sophistication, length, clarity, and tone across cases. Some customers are precise; some are rambling, use shorthand, misspell things, or bury the important detail in the third sentence. Never state the internal root cause, resolution type, issue subcategory, or team name verbatim — those are back-office labels the customer has never seen. Only reference the symptoms, environment, impact, and (if given) the customer's own theory/misdiagnosis.

Follow the "narrative_instruction" field for each case exactly.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"cases": [{"i": <int>, "title": "...", "description": "..."}, ...]} covering every case index in the input, in any order.

[{'i': 0, 'product_customer_sees': 'SSO Integration Module', 'environment': 'staging', 'region': 'US-West', 'symptoms_observed': ['duplicate account created', 'bulk import fully failed'], 'reported_business_impact': 'none', 'reported_affected_users': 0, 'narrative_instruction': 'Write a clear, reasonably well-organized ticket. The customer describes what they observed accurately and with enough detail to act on.'}]

response: {"cases": [{"i": 0, "title": "Duplicate accounts created and bulk import failed during SSO setup", "description": "We ran a bulk import of users into the SSO Integration Module in our staging environment, and it didn't work as expected. First, the entire import process failed with no error messages in the UI. Then, when we checked the database, we found that duplicate accounts had been created for about 20% of the entries that were partially processed before the failure. This is blocking our testing for the SSO rollout. Can someone please investigate why the import failed and why duplicates were created?"}]}
